findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: A filename containing a command substitution or a semicolon
findings.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate the filename before using it with fopen, which could allow for command injection if the filename comes from an untrusted source.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: A file content containing a command substitution or a semicolon
findings.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate the file content before using it with gcry_sexp_new, which could allow for command injection if the file content comes from an untrusted source.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: A very large filesize that causes malloc to fail or allocate less memory than expected
findings.assumptions: The code does not check if malloc returns NULL after allocating memory for filecontent, which could lead to a buffer overflow if the file content is larger than expected.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: A very large file that causes ftell to return a negative value or wrap around
findings.assumptions: The code does not check if ftell returns a negative value, which could lead to incorrect memory allocation and buffer overflow.
